habitat: Semi-arid and arid plains, sparse grassland, dry pans, burnt ground and fallow fields, usually on pale sandy or calcrete soils. Eastern records are sporadic.
summary: A small nomadic sparrow-lark of the arid west, only sporadic farther east. The male has a grey back and a strongly patterned black-and-white head, including a small white cap. The female is pale grey-brown, with light breast streaking, unstreaked flanks and a black patch on the lower belly. Immatures resemble the female but are variably spotted buff and white above. Chick down is not described. A Kruger month list is not given in the texts used here.

similar.note: Chestnut-backed Sparrow-Lark has chestnut wing coverts and grey underwings. Grey-backed Sparrow-Lark has a grey or sandy-grey back, and the male has a white cap.

viewNotes.note: Grey upperparts on the male. The male’s display is a circling song flight 15–30 m up, often with the legs dangling. A spread upperwing colour is not described.
The underwing is not described. Flocks fly up with a chirping flight call.
The male’s head is black and white, with a small white cap. The female’s breast is lightly streaked.
The male’s back is grey, which is the mark against the other sparrow-larks. The female’s back is pale grey-brown.
Male: white cap and black-and-white face on a grey back. Female: pale grey-brown, with a black patch on the lower belly.

calls.description: Flocks give shrill chirps while feeding, and a chirping call in flight; the texts used here do not assign these calls to one sex.
The singing male circles in a series of undulations, often with the legs dangling. The texts used here do not transcribe that song.

research.note: No Kemp figure is stored, and that population object is unchanged. SABAP1 and the Biodiversity and Development Institute describe nomadic movements and irruptions into the east, and do not give a Kruger month list, so months and a movement status are omitted. The male’s underpart colours, apart from the black-and-white head, are not spelled out. The best non-ND call is grade B from the Eastern Cape. Grade A files for this species in the catalogue used here were ND and were not used. The display song has no recording. The iNaturalist account name is wildguide-.
